judge_context:
Executive Summary
The paper introduces EcoEvoApps, an open-source R package designed to bridge the gap between theoretical and empirical ecology by providing interactive simulations of fundamental models. Addressing the barrier where mathematical models seem foreign to empiricists, the authors developed 11 Shiny apps covering topics like predator-prey dynamics and island biogeography. These apps allow users to manipulate parameters and visualize outcomes, serving as both standalone educational tools and a gateway to R programming. The study evaluated the apps in undergraduate classrooms at UCLA and the University of Missouri, surveying 51 students who used the tools for guided exploration. Results showed that an overwhelming majority of students found the apps moderately to very helpful for understanding model structures and specific concepts like carrying capacity. Furthermore, tracking individual student interest and confidence revealed substantial gains, particularly among those with higher initial interest. The package is freely available, open-source, and includes functions for direct simulation and plotting, aiming to foster collaboration and deeper conceptual understanding in the EEB community.

Research Context
Integrating theory with observations is a fundamental driver of progress in life sciences. Mathematical models enable generalization and deeper conceptual understanding of biological systems. There is widespread agreement that synergism between empiricists and theoreticians yields fruitful insights. Equation-heavy papers are often cited less, creating a barrier to integration for empiricists. Instructors of quantitative courses tend to receive worse student evaluations than those who de-emphasize quantitative topics. Existing calls for quantitative training focus primarily on statistical models or programming skills. Interactive tools that allow users to independently explore model structure help increase student interest and understanding.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aims to describe EcoEvoApps, an open-source package providing interactive apps for fundamental EEB models. The authors hypothesize that these apps will facilitate communication and collaboration between theoretical and empirical researchers. The apps are expected to help individuals gain familiarity with models and assist in large undergraduate classroom settings. The authors predict that interactive exploration will reveal the logic behind complex model conclusions, such as the paradox of enrichment. It is hypothesized that using interactive apps in classrooms will lead to substantial gains in student confidence and understanding. The authors expect the package to grow as a collaborative and inclusive effort within the EEB community. The study anticipates that R and Shiny will provide easier access to theoretical insights than years of quantitative training.

Methodological Details
The package includes 11 interactive apps chosen by surveying syllabi for undergraduate ecology courses and textbooks. Models were selected based on commonly-used textbooks like Gotelli (2008) and Begon and Townsend (2020). Some apps implement specific model dynamics, while others present several closely related models. A core set of nine apps are available in English, Spanish, Chinese, Turkish, and Portuguese. The apps are freely available online on RStudio's shinyapps.io servers or can be launched locally from the R console. The package provides functions with the prefix shiny_ to launch apps directly from the R console. To evaluate value in classrooms, the authors surveyed 51 students who used the apps for Island Biogeography and Lotka-Volterra competition. The learning activity included short video lectures followed by a worksheet navigating students through a guided exploration. Students rated on a scale of 1-7 the degree to which the apps helped them understand the model as a whole. Similar surveys were conducted for students in a General Ecology course at the University of Missouri. Individual students' interest and confidence in models were tracked before and after the activity. Classroom surveys were reviewed by the UCLA Institutional Review Board and MU Institutional Review Board.

Procedures And Architectures
The package is an open-source R package (ecoevoapps) with a website at https://ecoevoapps.gitlab.io. Under the hood, Shiny apps use functions in the ecoevoapps package to simulate and visualize model dynamics. Simulations are conducted by functions with the prefix run_, which take parameter values and initial population sizes as input. The run_ functions return a dataframe of the population sizes for each species over the specified time series. The package includes plotting functions prefixed plot_ that take the object returned by the corresponding run_ function. The plot_ functions return a ggplot2 object to visualize the simulation results. The complete list of functions for simulating and plotting model dynamics is provided in Table 1. Each function's usage is documented in the package, and suites of functions relevant to different models are described in vignettes. Users can customize and deploy their own instance of an app for hosting on institutional servers. The package includes model-specific vignettes with instructions for simulating the model dynamics directly through R.

Key Results
An overwhelming majority of students (40/51) reported that the apps were moderately to very helpful for learning the models as a whole. Students reported that they better understand concepts like carrying capacity or coexistence after using the Lotka-Volterra competition app. Using interactive apps led to substantial gains in student confidence, especially among students who express higher interest in related topics. Low values of prey carrying capacity result in a stationary equilibrium or one with stable oscillations. High values of prey carrying capacity result in unstable oscillations that ultimately limit the system's persistence. Careful exploration of the parameter K can reveal the logic behind the conclusion that the system can persist only when the equilibrium point occurs to the right of the hump. The apps allow users to visualize the paradox of enrichment by altering the value of the prey carrying capacity. The package serves as a gateway for users to implement and manipulate mathematical models at the command line.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Interactive tools help increase student interest and understanding of quantitative concepts in ecology and evolutionary biology. Platforms like R and Shiny allow building tools that give everyone easier access to theoretical insights. EcoEvoApps is entirely open-source and written in R, making it easily accessible and customizable by others in the EEB community. The package aims to facilitate communication and collaboration between theoretical and empirical researchers. The study suggests that simulation-based learning can provide insights that otherwise take years of quantitative training to grasp. The authors plan to prioritize incorporating mathematical models from evolutionary biology and population genetics into the package.

Contradictions And Limitations
The study relies on self-reported survey data from students, which may be subject to bias. The evaluation was limited to two specific courses (UCLA and MU) and may not generalize to all EEB contexts. The paper notes that simulation-based learning may not provide all the same insights as analytical solutions. The package is currently focused on ecological models, with evolutionary biology and population genetics models planned for future releases. The paper does not report specific statistical significance tests for the survey results, only descriptive counts and percentages.

Claims
Interactive apps significantly improve student understanding and confidence in theoretical ecological models. An overwhelming majority of students (40/51) reported that the apps were moderately to very helpful. Using interactive apps led to substantial gains in student confidence. Simulation-based learning may not provide all the same insights as analytical solutions. Interactive tools can facilitate communication and collaboration between theoretical and empirical researchers.
EcoEvoApps serves as an accessible gateway for users to implement and manipulate mathematical models. The package can also serve as a gateway for users to implement and manipulate mathematical models at the command line. Users can customize and deploy their own instance of an app for hosting on institutional servers.  The package is easily accessible and customizable by others in the EEB community.

Data And Code Availability
The package is an open-source R package (ecoevoapps) available on GitLab. The shiny apps are freely available online on RStudio's shinyapps.io servers.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Similar surveys were conducted at the University of Missouri with similar results. The package includes functions to directly run models through the R console, serving as a bridge to coding.
